clue.text: Making silly faces but not extremely easily

indicators.note: making here means fashioning something new out of the letters of the phrase, a remaking that signals a rearrangement
not extremely tells us to drop the letters at the very ends of the phrase silly faces

explanation.surface: Someone pulls daft faces, though not to excess, and does it without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not extremely' removes the first and last letters of 'silly faces' (S and S), leaving ILLYFACE; 'Making' then rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a facile way means doing it with little effort, so the adverb is a synonym of easily.

clue.text: Marvellous article about one member of Society

indicators.note: about means the first two pieces wrap around the letter for one

parts.note: fab is slang for fabulous, marvellous
an is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wonderful piece written about a single member of high society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Society is the Fabian Society, the British socialist group, not high society; the capital S gives it away.
explanation.definitionFit: The British socialist think tank founded in 1884 takes its name from the Roman general Fabius, and its members bear his name.

clue.text: Many cheat in order to get distinction

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

indicators.note: in order suggests the letters of cheat being put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Lots of people cheat to win honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges CHEAT into ACHET.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet means prestige or a mark of distinction.

clue.text: Evangelical in the old' city, among vulgar companions

indicators.note: among means the city's name is placed in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: low means coarse or vulgar
CH stands for Companion of Honour; the plural gives it twice
CH stands for Companion of Honour; the plural gives it twice
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A gospel preacher in an ancient city keeps coarse company.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour is a British order whose holders use the letters after their names; 'among' puts the ancient city between the two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The wing of the Church of England that stresses gospel preaching over ritual is the evangelical wing.

clue.text: Lack of enthusiasm for schedule with fifty points

parts.note: a schedule is a list
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
points of the compass: E, S, S, N, E, S, S

explanation.surface: Someone has no appetite for a timetable with fifty items on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points, seven of them strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy and lethargy are both a want of energy or interest.

clue.text: Energetic person receives pound fine, as a driver of course

indicators.note: receives means the word for the energetic person takes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: a goer is a lively, energetic person
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A lively individual is handed a pound fine, presumably for speeding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'driver' a motorist and 'course' a filler; in fact the driver is a golf club and the course a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is the long club teed off with, so a player wielding one on the links fits the description.

clue.text: Old game, arranged as the last of a series

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of game are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned game set up as the final one of a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reshuffles the four letters of the game word, placed after the abbreviation for 'Old'; 'Old game' reads as a pastime but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end of any sequence.

clue.text: Brilliant regiment, absent from footdrill manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres signals that the letters of footdrill are moved about into a new order

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for regiment

explanation.surface: A sparkling regiment that skipped its parade-ground exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R (regiment) out of FOOTDRILL and rearrange what is left, as 'manoeuvres' instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium lit by powerful lamps is brilliantly illuminated.

clue.text: Unsociable practice arising in the band

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the word for band

parts.note: a ring is a band, as a wedding band

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means the word reads upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial practice

explanation.surface: Antisocial habits are emerging among the musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns RITE upward to ETIR, which goes into RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy person is reserved and avoids company, which is unsociable.

clue.text: Repercussions of help in the bath?

definitions.meaning: after-effects or consequences that follow an event
a playful reading: someone scrubbing the part of you that you cannot reach while bathing

explanation.surface: Wondering what comes of offering assistance at bath time.
explanation.definitionFit: Repercussions are consequences rippling out, like the wave behind a boat; and helping a bather means scrubbing behind them.

clue.text: Go often to Brighton, for example

definitions.meaning: to frequent a place, visiting it habitually
Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast, a classic holiday destination

explanation.surface: A suggestion to pay frequent visits to Brighton or somewhere like it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have recourse to a place habitually is one sense; the other is a holiday town by the sea, as Brighton on England's south coast is.

clue.text: Admitting all doubt, it's anyone's guess

parts.note: a place open to everyone admits all comers
doubt is uncertainty, a query raised over something

explanation.surface: Confessing every uncertainty, since nobody really knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitting' suggests confessing but means letting in.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter not yet settled is undecided, so any guess is as good as another.

clue.text: Beginning in Israel, the sacred river keeps East

indicators.note: keeps means the river's name holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: Alph is 'the sacred river' of Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Israel a holy river rises and holds to an eastward course.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Beginning' as a river's source in Israel; it is really the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet is the starting point of writing used in Israel.

clue.text: Polish and German states North European, of course

parts.note: to lap a gem or lens is to polish it
the Länder are the federal states of Germany

explanation.surface: Polish territory and German regions make up a stretch of northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the verb. The German states are its Länder, written without the umlaut.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the far north of Scandinavia and Finland is a northern European by birth.

clue.text: Introduction to a lecture

definitions.meaning: the formal act of introducing one person to another, as at court
a talk given to an audience, often with slides

explanation.surface: The opening words before a talk is given.
explanation.definitionFit: Being formally introduced at court is one sense, and a talk delivered to an audience is the other.

clue.text: A remedy for many in depression, after the end of prayers

indicators.note: after means the word ending prayers comes first and the rest follows it

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer

indicators.note: in means the letter for many goes inside the word for depression

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, i.e. many

explanation.surface: A cure for a lot of people feeling low, once prayers are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of prayers' is the word said at their close, not their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A correction to a text or a law puts right a fault, so it is a remedy.

clue.text: How to play .troublesome toccatas?

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the letters of toccatas are disturbed into another order

explanation.surface: Asking how to perform some difficult keyboard pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Toccatas are fast, showy keyboard pieces, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction for detached, clipped notes, telling a player how to perform a passage.

clue.text: "Hell is full of musical" (G B Shaw)

definitions.text: "Hell is full of musical" (G B Shaw)

parts.words: Hell is full of musical" (G B Shaw)
parts.note: complete Shaw's line from Man and Superman: the missing word names non-professional performers

explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's quip says the inferno is crowded with unpaid, unskilled music-makers, people who play for love rather than money.

clue.text: Paid on occasion, as established by custom

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: an occasion is a time, as in 'on that occasion'
a cheque or bill is met in full when the bank pays it out

explanation.surface: Money handed over on a particular date, as tradition demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid' is the sense used of a cheque the bank accepts and pays, not money simply handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hallowed by long tradition is respected because it has lasted, which is what established by custom means.

clue.text: Face up to girl clutching wooden skittle

indicators.note: clutching means the girl's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
a pin is a skittle, as in ninepins

explanation.surface: Confronting a girl who is gripping a skittle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face up' looks like 'confront', but it means lying on one's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying on the back with the front turned to the sky is the posture meant.

clue.text: Foreign currency group invested in plant

indicators.note: invested in means the group is put inside the word for plant

parts.note: the pea is a climbing plant
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A consortium has put money into a factory abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks industrial and 'invested' financial; it is the garden pea, wrapped round SET.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the money of Spain before the euro, so a currency from abroad.

clue.text: Old crooks ignore contracts

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
to purse the lips is to contract them

explanation.surface: Former villains pay no attention to their legal agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' is the verb (draws together), not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: These were thieves of past centuries who sliced through the strings of a victim's money bag, hence crooks of old.

clue.text: 'Affect drastically when at university on purpose

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
an end is a purpose or aim

explanation.surface: Someone changes things radically when at college, and does it deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' for at university is British: students go up to Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn something, literally turning it on its head, is to affect it drastically.

clue.text: Put out some tremendous entertainment

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a spectacular show gets extinguished.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit at the end of 'tremendous' and the start of 'entertainment'.
explanation.definitionFit: To extinguish a fire or light, especially with water, is to put it out.

clue.text: A hint about headmaster's new judgement

indicators.note: about means the word for a hint goes round the other letter

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint
read as head + master: the head (first letter) of 'master' is M

explanation.surface: A school head drops a hint about a fresh verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headmaster's' is split as 'head' of 'master', giving M; the cue's hint goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is shrewdness or keen insight, the faculty of judging well.

clue.text: Too prudent to follow fancy

indicators.note: to follow means the word for prudent comes after the word for fancy

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
wise means sensible or prudent

explanation.surface: Someone too sensible to chase a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too' looks like an adverb of excess; it means 'also'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean 'in the same way, also', so they swap freely in a sentence.

clue.text: A chap imprisoned by one in a lawful position

indicators.note: imprisoned by means the chap's name is locked up inside the word for one

parts.note: taken as written
Sid is a typical man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man is jailed by somebody who claims to be on the right side of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby a player in a lawful position relative to the ball is not offside.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who is not offside stands where the rules allow, so is lawfully placed.

clue.text: Anecdotes — the academic's curse!

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a person
taken as written
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree, standing for an academic

explanation.surface: An academic's anecdotes are a torment to listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of anecdotes, is crossword shorthand worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ban or ecclesiastical curse; also something loathed.
